subject: Data boundary handshake + just-in-time egress protocol for EU workloads
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@elara-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@elara-health.com
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency & DPA — question on boundary handback / JIT egress

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal and infra teams asked for a clear description of how Redwood handles EU customer data when there is a transient processing need outside the EU (for example, cache rehydration or a short DR window). Specifically:

- Can Redwood commit to data-at-rest residency in eu-west-1 for Elara production datasets?
- For any necessary short-term cross-region processing, do you provide an "acceptance/handshake" window (SLA) and a logging trail showing which records were touched?
- We need a roster of subprocessors and a proposed timeline for onboarding new ones (30/60/90 days or shorter).

If you can send a DPA draft and a short operational playbook or diagram describing the JIT egress flow, that would help speed our internal review.

Attaching a requirements checklist in a separate mail from procurement.

Best,
Sara
Senior PM, Data Privacy — Elara Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@elara-health.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@elara-health.com
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & DPA — question on boundary handback / JIT egress

Hi Sara —

Thanks, happy to take this on. Attached is a first-pass DPA draft and a short FAQ that explains our operational model for locality and transient processing. Highlights up front:

- We can anchor customer data at rest to a chosen region (eu-west-1) for production datasets and keys.
- Short-duration processing outside the anchor region ("just-in-time egress") is supported only for three discrete cases: cache warm-up after a full restore, scheduled multi-region analytics jobs you opt into, and emergency failover.
- Each transient event is logged with a unique event id; we retain audit records for 13 months by default (can be extended).
- Subprocessor roster is attached; new subprocessors have a minimum 30-day notification, and critical infra changes trigger a 7-day expedited notice if we must onboard for security/fix reasons.

I'll loop in our infra lead to explain the mechanics. If you want stricter windows for onboarding, we can propose a committed SLA in the DPA addendum section.

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: subprocessors_roster_2026-04.csv (csv)

Thanks — talk soon.

Subject: Re: Residency & DPA — question on boundary handback / JIT egress

Hi Sara — copying the infra notes here so you have visibility into the exact mechanics.

Operational summary (technical):
- Anchor storage: Production object stores and KMS keys for Elara will be provisioned in eu-west-1 and locked to the tenancy. Backups are stored in the same region unless you opt into cross-region replication.
- JIT egress flow: when a cache or model KV page is missing and we warm from cold storage, the request is handled in-region; if capacity constraints require a temporary worker outside eu-west-1 we will:
  1) open a transient worker with a narrow ACL for the exact shard(s),
  2) generate an event id and record the diff + audit metadata,
  3) clear KV caches and revoke the worker within the configured window (default 4 hours).
- Audit & evidence: full per-event audit (event id, start/end timestamps, IP, instance id, operator) exported as CSV/JSON and available via Console + .csv export.
- Subprocessors: the roster attached to Marissa's note is accurate; any non-critical subprocessor additions follow the 30/30 notice/onboard timeline. For critical security-patch-driven vendors we have a 7-day emergency lane with post-facto attestation and evidence.

Questions for Elara to confirm:
- Acceptable maximum transient window (we default 4 hours);
- Whether you need per-record hashing in the audit or record-level redaction before log export;
- Desired retention for audit logs (13 months default).

Attachment: subprocessors_roster_2026-04.csv (ref)

Karthik Iyer
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed the DPA and attached our redlines. Main asks from legal/infosec:

- We need a hard SLA for the transient worker window (Elara requests max 2 hours) and a contractual commitment to revoke any worker earlier when the task completes.
- Evidence: every transient event must produce an exportable proof bundle (event id, start/end, instance ids, and the exact list of records touched or a hashed list).
- Subprocessor timeline: we prefer a 14-day notice for non-critical additions and require an explicit approval right for any subprocessor located outside the EU.

Attached: redlines_elara.docx (docx)

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the 2-hour cap, the proof-bundle format, and the 14-day notice/approval right.

Tom Barrett
Legal Counsel — Elara Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & DPA — question on boundary handback / JIT egress

Tom / team — appreciate the detailed redlines. Summary of Redwood's proposed concessions and next actions: 

Concessions (proposed for DPA addendum):
- Transient worker window: Redwood will accept a 2-hour contractual cap for scheduled/non-emergency JIT events. Emergency DR events retain a separate exception lane with prior notification obligations; those will be enumerated in the addendum.
- Proof bundle: we will provide an exportable proof bundle with event id, start/end timestamps, instance ids, and a hashed per-record list (SHA-256) to preserve minimal exposure while enabling verification. Format: newline-delimited JSON, available via Console export.
- Subprocessor approvals: Redwood will commit to a 14-day notice and will require explicit written approval for any subprocessor physically located outside the EU for Elara-bound workloads. Non-EU subprocessors required for security patches will follow the emergency lane with post-event evidence and a post-hoc approval workflow.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Redwood legal to incorporate concessions into a DPA addendum (we'll send a redline by EOD 2026-05-06).
2) Karthik to publish the proof-bundle schema and a sample export (ETA 2026-05-07).
3) Elara to confirm acceptance of emergency lane language and whether you want audit retention longer than 13 months.
4) Execute DPA + addendum, then sign-off with procurement.
